title: Mediterranean Halibut and Tomato Skillet
intro: This satisfying skillet meal relies on blistered cherry tomatoes to build a flavorful pan sauce. The savory broth simmers the lean halibut and perfectly seasons the whole-wheat couscous.

ingredients.name: Cherry tomatoes
ingredients.canonical_name: Tomatoes, red, ripe, raw, year round average

ingredients.name: Low-sodium vegetable broth
ingredients.canonical_name: Soup, vegetable broth, ready to serve

instructions: Place the couscous in a heatproof bowl. Pour in the boiling water, cover tightly, let sit for 5 minutes to hydrate, and fluff with a fork.
Season the halibut with the dried oregano, black pepper, and salt.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the halibut for 3 to 4 minutes on one side until golden, flip the fish, and transfer to a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the cherry tomatoes and garlic to the skillet. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes begin to blister and burst.
Pour in the vegetable broth, scraping up any browned bits from the pan. Stir in the spinach and olives, cooking for 1 to 2 minutes until the spinach wilts.
Return the halibut to the skillet. Simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, spooning the tomato sauce over the fish, until the fish is completely opaque and flakes easily.
Remove the skillet from the heat and pour in the lemon juice. Serve the halibut and blistered tomato sauce over the steamed couscous.
variation: Swap the halibut for an equal amount of peeled shrimp.
conservation: Keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat gently on the stovetop.
